newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA SEBI SUSPENDS 17 PUNE BROKERS.
newsitem.headline: INDIA SEBI SUSPENDS 17 PUNE BROKERS.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Wednesday that it had suspended 17 brokers at the Pune exchange for periods ranging from three months to a year beginning September 1 for trading violations.
In one case, the market watchdog said it had cancelled the registration of broker Mangal Jain.
SEBI said the brokers had indulged in "unauthorised carry forward transactions and consequent depression of prices" on the exchange between October 1995 and January 1996.
Five other brokers -- Rajendra Daga, Mayur Investments, Bhojwani Securities, J.P. Surana and Devi Investments -- were let off with a warning, SEBI said in a statement.
Two brokerages suspended for a year are Pratik Investments and Janhavi Securities Private Ltd, it said.

The brokers suspended for three months are: H.A. Shah, Bindu Patni, Elite Securities, RBM Investments, Mayfair Investments and Consultancy Services, Rajesh A Parikh, Clever Investment and Securities Private Ltd, S.T. Shah, Rachna Consultants, Kunal Securities Private Ltd, Prabodh Arthwardhini Private Ltd, Paresh Mehta, Vardi Rathod, Jitendra Wagh and Rajesh Kasat.
